item.title: Mon, Nov. 02 Electoral Vote Predictor
item.content:encoded:
We are not going to have a run down of all the elections today. We are saving that for tomorrow. Don't miss it. Then at 6 pm EST (7 pm EDT if you prefer Daylight Saving Time all year) tomorrow we will switch to Nov. 4 and start live blogging the election all night until it's over or we run out of coffee. We will frequently update the main page, but you will have to force a reload of the page regularly to see the new page. See how here.

And a reminder that we are running a survey, so that readers can predict which candidate they think will win the 18 Senate races that are plausibly in doubt, how many House seats the Democrats will win, and which candidate they think will win the 17 gubernatorial races that are plausibly in doubt.The survey will be available until 10:00 p.m. PT tonight; we will have the results in Tuesday's posting. Click here to record your responses.

Don't Confuse Them Losing with Us Winning

Democrats are very nervous. The news is all good and they can't believe it. Texas is in play? South Carolina is in play? Kansas is in play? It makes no sense. They are panicking that half the Republicans refuse to be polled and that the polls are way off. Nate Silver ran this cartoon to express Democrats' feelings.

item.title: Sun, Nov. 01 Electoral Vote Predictor
item.content:encoded:
It was VERY late, for various reasons, but there WAS a posting yesterday, and a substantive one. This posting is the sequel, in a manner of speaking, as we explained yesterday.

Also, we have put together a survey, so that readers can predict which candidate they think will win the 18 Senate races that are plausibly in doubt, how many House seats the Democrats will win, and which candidate they think will win the 17 gubernatorial races that are plausibly in doubt. There is also a space to make one other prediction, of any type, for Tuesday, for those readers who have thoughts. The survey will be available until 10:00 p.m. PT Monday night; we will have the results in Tuesday's posting. Click here to record your responses. We thank reader S.A.K. in Karnataka, India, for reminding us to do this.

And finally, a (belated) congratulations to the Milwaukee Brewers on their first World Series win, and congratulations to the Golden State Valkyries on their first WNBA title.

item.title: Sat, Oct. 31 Electoral Vote Predictor
item.content:encoded:
Sigh. You know what they say about the best laid plans of mice and men.

It took us a very long time to put today's posting together. That is in substantial part because it's quite long, over 9,000 words. And we only kept it to 9,000 words because we held two items that were supposed to be here.

We're going to move those two items to Sunday. We'll also have some Local Bytes and some questions and answers. It's supposed to be non-politics questions weekend, but we think we have to do serious questions when there is a major election looming. We'll do non-politics questions either next weekend, or the weekend thereafter, depending on how the elections go.

To the many and varied people who have sent in e-mails of complaint—some of them very sharply worded—about our schedule this weekend, there is only so much we can do. It takes time to write this material, particularly when it is complicated stuff. We're also preparing for Tuesday, and have been dealing with some tech issues related to that process. And, oh yeah, we have non-blog responsibilities. We do our best to produce the best work we can, while not risking (further) illness. The complaints do not accomplish anything.

Meanwhile, even what time it is has become intensely political, like everything else. Nevertheless, we still recommend that you set your clocks back an hour tonight, no matter whether you are a Democrat, Republican, independent or something else.

And finally, Happy Halloween from staff canine/bat Tuco, and the rest of us at Electoral-Vote.com!

item.content:encoded:
Inflation Is Bad... Wonder Why?

March was not a great month for Americans' pocketbooks, as monthly inflation tripled, from 0.3% per month to 0.9% per month. This means the overall inflation rate jumped from 2.4% to 3.3%. This will not be good news for any politician or political party in line to be blamed for the nation's economic woes.

Saturday Q&amp;A

By the standards of the Trump presidency, it was actually a somewhat light news week. That makes for a much more diverse Q&A, since the questions are not dominated by one or two particular subjects.

And for anyone still working on this week's headline theme, we'll say that, like Richard I of England, the magicians Siegfried and Roy would do well with this theme, if they weren't dead.

We're working through a bit of technical trouble with e-mail, and don't want to wait until too late to post this. So, the last set of London recommendations will run next week.
